title: Minimum Knight Moves
summary: On an infinite chessboard, starting at [0, 0], a knight must reach [x, y] using the least number of moves.
statement: On an infinite chessboard, starting at [0, 0], a knight must reach [x, y] using the least number of moves. A knight can move two squares in a cardinal direction followed by one square orthogonally. The solution guarantees a minimum step count exists.
constraints: The board is infinite and coordinates may be negative.
Return the minimum number of knight moves from (0,0).
hints: Reflect the target into the nonnegative quadrant using symmetry.
Breadth-first search guarantees the first visit has minimum move count.
Allow coordinates down to -2 because shortest paths near the axes may briefly cross them; upper bounds need only target+2.
All farther excursions can be reflected or shortened, so the bounded BFS retains an optimal route.
editorial: All farther excursions can be reflected or shortened, so the bounded BFS retains an optimal route.

tests.explanation: A knight reaches 2,1 in one move.
A shortest route requires four moves.
